mentl/152b527:
Went to build the handle change and the arithmetic refuted it first, which is
the design pass doing its job rather than an OOM doing it later.

THE SUBSTRATE ALREADY DECOMPOSES A HANDLE. graph.mn:96-100:

    let spine_slots = 16384
    fn spine_band(h) = h / spine_slots
    fn spine_slot(h) = h % spine_slots

and pages open on demand via spine_ensure, so a sparse handle space costs only
the pages actually touched. The page structure was built FOR this — its own
comment: "mint distribution (max 2,305 mints per decl on the wheel, p99 331 —
7x headroom for the per-decl banding this page structure carries next)". So
(arena, offset) is not a new mechanism at all; per-decl banding is band = decl
index, and the 3,385 top-level decls of the wheel are the arenas.

THE REFUTATION. spine_open_loop (graph.mn:129-135) allocates a page with
TWELVE columns, each make_list(spine_slots), and make_list(n) = alloc_list(n)
(lib/lists.mn:110) is eager. One page is therefore 12 x 16,384 slots. One band
per decl is 3,385 pages = ~665M slots = ~2.66GB of spine alone, against a
measured 2.4GB whole-compile peak. Naive per-decl banding roughly doubles the
image.

TWO PREREQUISITES, both deletions, both measurable:

1. SIZE THE BAND FROM THE MEASURED DISTRIBUTION. p99 is 331, not 16384. A
   512-slot band puts per-decl banding at ~83MB with overflow bands for the
   ~1% tail. Total memory is unchanged for the dense case — it is
   (pages x slots) either way — so the only waste is each band's unused tail.
   The 16384 figure was sized so ONE page holds the worst decl (16384/2305 =
   7.1x). That is the right sizing for a DENSE handle space and the wrong one
   for a per-decl space, where the cost is paid 3,385 times instead of ~40.

2. LAZY COLUMNS. Twelve dense columns allocated eagerly for a page whose
   sparse columns the readers already guard ("a spine_open guard for the
   sparse columns", graph.mn:103) is the same over-allocation disease one
   layer down, and it is independent of this

perennials/15d14ee:
A yard has always assumed flat ground in silence: the sheet, the
elevation and the model all stood everything on one level nobody chose.
This adds the terrain the three projections were missing one record of:
Yard.ground, spot heights in metres relative to the level she calls
zero, hers entirely, capped and sanitized like every other mark.

lib/ground.ts is the single interpolator every projection will read, so
they cannot disagree about where the ground stands. The surface passes
exactly through every mark, bends smoothly between neighbours, and
settles back to level where she marked nothing, because absence claims
nothing. It also computes the side-on skyline and the section scale the
elevation and the exported band will share.

The sun learns the same shape: crowns lift by the ground under them, a
bed point stands at its own footing, and the land itself can shade — a
coarse march over the height field, stopping at the sheet's edge because
the sheet claims nothing about ground it does not hold. All optional
parameters, so a flat yard computes exactly as before.

Nine new rules pin the honesty: exact at her marks, bounded between
them, settling to level beyond them, a typo never folds the scale, an
old yard gains no key, and a winter bank shades the bed behind it while
a distant molehill shades nothing.
bits/1553901:
Passes now start from a scrubbable playhead: the sim fast-forwards to
the punch-in point on the same fixed-step grid, so a pass recorded over
the ending is exactly what a full replay produces. The preview clock
rides the AudioContext instead of wall time, so mouths flap on the
audio's schedule.

Who's talking becomes something you perform: once a mouthed puppet has
passes, it speaks only while one covers the moment, and a fresh cast
still flaps freely so the first mouth lands with instant feedback.
Still-holds sample periodically, so holding the talker without moving
is a valid talk span. Passes can also target a snipped-off piece: the
dangle's spring chases the performed point through the joint's world
position and settles back to gravity when the pass ends. Googly eyes
lag the motion with seeded jitter and ride their piece like mouths do.

The sim precomputes per-puppet pass tables instead of rescanning the
event log every step. Camera capture casts straight from the lens;
undo gains redo; bits rename from the list; deleting a bit reclaims
its audio and cutout assets; renders hold a wake lock. 27 unit tests
and the e2e fixture (now with eyes and a piece pass) stay green.
